government.note: Semi-presidential republic under the 1992 Constitution. The directly elected President (modified two-round system, five-year term renewable once consecutively) represents the country internationally and appoints the Prime Minister with the approval of the Seimas, with more executive authority than the Estonian and Latvian presidents; the Government led by the Prime Minister needs the confidence of the 141-member Seimas. On a vacancy the Speaker of the Seimas acts as President (Artūras Paulauskas in 2004). Constitutional referendums require a majority of all registered voters, which caused the 2019 and 2024 proposals to fail.

system.note: Parallel voting: 71 single-member constituencies (two-round majority system, except in 2000) and 70 seats from nationwide lists allocated by largest remainder with a 5% threshold (7% for coalitions since 1996). seats_2000 is the result of the 1996 election; changes in group membership between 1996 and 1 January 2000 were not checked. Others: Young Lithuania, Christian Democratic Union, Lithuanian Citizens' Alliance, Political Prisoners and Deportees (1 each) and the Nationalist-Democratic list (3).
